title: Administration
subtitle: Manage access, members and invites.
organizationSubtitle: Manage people, access, operating data, and the systems your workspace depends on.
removeBody: This deletes their account and revokes access immediately. This can’t be undone.
approveElevatedBody: This approves {name} with the {role} role, not just employee access. Make sure that's intended.
externalMembersHint: Members whose email is outside your company domains. They have full access according to their role.
inviteExternalHint: External address — they'll be invited as a full member with the selected role.
inviteExternalBody: {email} is outside your company domains. They'll receive a Clerk invitation and get full access as the selected role. Send it anyway?
onboardBannerDescription: Set up access — with a personal or company email.
onboardPageDescription: Set up access, depending on whether a personal or a company email address is used.
onboardPersonalIntro: Recommended path: a personal email address works exactly the same for intranet access — you can start right away, without waiting on IT to set up a company mailbox first. The person just signs in with the invited address. A company address can always be added later.
onboardCompanyIntro1: A company email address needs to be set up with IT or your email provider first, before the person can sign in with it — that can take a bit of time.
onboardCompanyIntro2: Once the address exists, the plain invite below is all you need. Department, team, and job title are then filled in by the person themselves in their own profile.
teamAccessDescription: Direct read-only OneDrive access to the Team folder, granted per employee — separate from the intranet's own upload-request flow.
teamAccessSynced: {granted} newly granted, {alreadyHadAccess} already had OneDrive access, {skipped} were already tracked.
teamAccessAlreadyHadAccess: Already has OneDrive access (role: {roles}) — left unchanged.
gfAccessTooltip: Has the Geschäftsführung allowlist flag — an independent OneDrive permission, not part of their role.
applicantDelegateBadgeTitle: Can grant Applicant Management access to others
roleLabelHint: Custom display name for this role badge (e.g. "Managing Director"). Permissions stay unchanged.
authenticationSubtitle: Company-wide sign-in requirements, and how they're enforced.
authenticationBannerMfaManagers: MFA required for managers and up
authenticationBannerPasskeyManagers: Passkey required for managers and up
authenticationBannerNonCompliant: {count, plural, one {# account non-compliant} other {# accounts non-compliant}}
authenticationStandardHint: Live adoption and who's currently short of the requirements below.
authenticationStandardNonCompliant: {count, plural, =0 {No non-compliant accounts} one {# account below the requirement} other {# accounts below the requirement}}
authenticationStandardClean: Everyone in scope currently meets the requirements below.
authenticationRetroactiveHint: Without this, only new accounts created from now on are affected — nobody who already has access gets interrupted.
authenticationMfaHint: Requires an authenticator app, a passkey, or an email code (weakest, still counts) before someone can use the intranet.
authenticationPasskeyHint: Requires at least one passkey registered on the account — the strongest sign-in method, and immune to phishing.
authenticationDestructiveHint: A separate, optional bar for actions like removing a member or issuing a password reset — independent of the sign-in requirement above.
authenticationDestructiveEnable: Require a fresh verification before sensitive actions
authenticationGracePeriodHint: Existing accounts newly brought into scope by a retroactive requirement get this many days as a soft warning before they're actually blocked. Set to 0 to enforce immediately.
authenticationExemptHint: These accounts are never blocked by any requirement above — for break-glass or shared accounts that can't set up MFA.
authenticationAreaStandardHint: Who's opted out of device recognition, and who's asked to always step up for a linked area instead of trusting the 14-day window below.
authenticationAreaReverifyHint: How long a password-less linked area (Performance, the HR vault) trusts a step-up before demanding a fresh one. Applies unless someone's own preference asks for a step-up every time.
authenticationLegacyPasswordHint: Once turned on, a fixed grace period starts immediately — the standalone password keeps working for that long, then stops for every account it applies to. This interrupts people who already have access; confirm before turning it on.
authenticationLegacyPasswordPerformanceH: Every Performance login linked to an intranet account loses its own password once the grace period ends — the intranet-account sign-in stays as the only way in.
authenticationLegacyPasswordApplicantVau: Every member with a passkey registered loses password-based vault unlock once the grace period ends — a member with no passkey is never affected.
authenticationConfirmBody: Existing accounts that don't meet the new requirement yet will be prompted the next time they open the site.
authenticationConfirmMfaRetroactive: Existing accounts without MFA will be asked to set it up
authenticationConfirmPasskeyRetroactive: Existing accounts without a passkey will be asked to add one
authenticationConfirmPerformanceSunset: Every linked Performance login will lose its standalone password once the grace period ends
authenticationConfirmApplicantVaultSunse: Every HR vault member with a passkey will lose password-based unlock once the grace period ends
requestsWaiting: {count, plural, one {# request waiting} other {# requests waiting}}
pendingInvites: {count, plural, one {# pending invite} other {# pending invites}}

orgEntity.introDepartments: cover everyone in one line of work, like Sales. Managers place people in a department.
orgEntity.introTeams: split a department into smaller groups, like Inbound inside Sales. Pick the department each team belongs to.
orgEntity.introLeads: — set who members report to. Someone on Inbound reports to the Inbound team lead and to the Sales department lead; both lines count.
orgEntity.introDirector: is marked by admins on a person's profile. It sits above everything but isn't a reporting line, and it adds to whatever else they are — a department lead can also be managing director.
orgEntity.departmentsDescription: Create, rename, or archive departments. Archiving keeps the department resolvable for members already assigned to it, but hides it from new assignments.
orgEntity.teamsDescription: Create, rename, or archive teams. Archiving keeps the team resolvable for existing members, but hides it from new assignments.
orgEntity.suggestionCategoriesDescription: Create, rename, or archive improvement-suggestion categories. Archiving keeps the category resolvable for existing suggestions, but hides it from new ones.
orgEntity.confirmArchiveBody: It stays resolvable for anyone already assigned to it, but disappears from new assignments until restored.
